name: Oman

facts.religion: Ibadi and Sunni Islam about 86%, Hindu and Christian expatriate minorities

snapshot: The Gulf's quiet mediator was hit by Iranian drones in 2026, then threatened by Trump over its talks with Tehran on managing the Strait of Hormuz.
culture: Oman is the only country where most Muslims follow Ibadism, a tolerant school distinct from Sunni and Shia Islam. Its forts, frankincense trade and a seafaring history that once stretched to Zanzibar shape identity. Omani men wear the dishdasha and khanjar dagger, which is on the flag. Ancient falaj irrigation channels still water oases.
society: Oil and gas provide most revenue, but reserves are smaller than its neighbours', so Oman introduced VAT and plans the Gulf's first income tax on high earners from 2028. Omanisation policies push citizens into private jobs held by foreigners. It has a tradition of quiet diplomacy, hosting secret US-Iran talks.
situation: Sultan Haitham bin Tarik succeeded his cousin Qaboos in 2020 and hosted US-Iran nuclear talks in 2025. When the war began on 28 February 2026, Iranian drones hit the ports of Duqm and Salalah, which US forces use, and other sites, reportedly killing 18 people; Tehran blamed rogue units. Oman kept talking to Iran, and in June the two agreed to work on a joint model for managing the Strait of Hormuz, prompting Trump to threaten to blow up Oman if it charged tolls. Its ports outside the strait have meanwhile boomed as alternatives to blocked Gulf hubs.
power: An absolute monarchy. The sultan is head of state, prime minister and commander of the armed forces; an elected consultative council and an appointed state council advise but cannot overrule him.

leaders.gov: The sultan also serves as prime minister
